correctness.rationale: The weighted prefix/block/tail decomposition p+h+e of d(x,y) is exact. Applied to (P_m-P_n)(delta_x-delta_y), finite 2-by-2 Kantorovich transport gives min(a+b,2p+h) for sources p_mx,p_ny and sinks p_nx,p_my. For p=0 the image ratio is <=1; otherwise p>=a_n and a,b<=B_{n,m}, yielding ratio <=2 min(1,B_{n,m}/a_n). A pair differing in one block coordinate gives ratio 1, and a min-prefix-coordinate pair with a common all-one block gives ratio 2 min(1,B_{n,m}/a_n). This works for m=infinity since weights are summable. Retractions P_n have norm 1, rank 2^n-1, commute, and strongly tend to I; the tail criterion follows exactly. Independent exact-rational all-molecule exhaustive checks on six finite weighted cube configurations verified 66 intervals and 18,648 ordered-as-unordered molecule pairs, with zero discrepancy; no extrapolation from finite tests was used.

value.rationale: The exact norm profile of every consecutive block of an explicit monotone FDD is a canonical quantitative invariant of that fixed decomposition. It distinguishes individual-block contractivity (geometric r<=1/2) from all-tail bimonotonicity (r<=1/3), giving a complete weight-sequence criterion absent from qualitative MAP or generic ||P_m-P_n||<=2. This is a motivated exact classification, not a broad basis optimality claim.

final_claim: For every strictly positive summable real weight sequence on K={0,1}^N, every coordinate interval retraction difference P_m-P_n with 1<=n<m<=infinity has norm max{1,2 min(1,B_{n,m}/a_n)}, with a_n=min_{j<=n}alpha_j, B_{n,m}=sum_{n<j<=m}alpha_j. Every P_m-P_0 has norm 1, and the canonical FDD is bimonotone exactly when sum_{j>n}alpha_j<=a_n/2 for every n.
